receipt
  • Read: Full text, version v2, indexed 2026-10-24
  • F1 Fig. 6 scores the "Heron noise model" against a real-hardware run with mean fidelity relative to a noiseless simulation, but every other result in the paper is scored on models the authors built (SI1000, uniform p, device-class models) and the logical error rates in the other figures come from stabilizer simulations, not from a device run.
  • F2 (a) 'reducing logical errors by an average of 81.92% from a grid' is a ratio of means dominated by the gross code (1.000 to 0.000). The mean of per-code reductions is 58.7% (our computation from the released results files). One code is 80% worse. (b) '69.14%' and '34.21%' each average two ratios of means, one at the original noise and one at the tenfold-reduced noise (15.29% and 122.98%, 13.27% and 55.15%). The mean of per-code single-QPU advantages is 12.69%.
  • F3 "universal improvements" (contradicted by Steane, 3.7 sd worse). "confirm"/"consistent" statements for 1000-shot single runs, many near the 0.5 ceiling. "negligible impact" for qubit variance with no width
  • F4 counts, fidelity numbers, calibration record and a device name in the text for Fig. 6 (the text says only "real hardware"). Source, chip, date and statistic (mean or median) of the Heron model constants. An interval on any logical error rate beyond the general statement of "confidence intervals" of about 0.004 for 1000 shots. The Zenodo record the paper cites holds one IBM job file (ibm_torino, submitted 2026-01-04, 60 circuits at 1000 shots) with no counts or fidelities, and the Heron constants appear there only as bare numbers in noise/heron_noise.py.

  • Read: Full text, version v1, indexed 2026-10-24
  • F1 Fig. 3's simulation check (legend r=0.9813) scores the estimator on "a holdout test ensemble [15] with an independent random seed", and the paper gives no difference between that ensemble and the training ensemble other than the seed. The training ensemble uses the variance scales of Table 1, of which the paper says "This choice is not claimed to be optimal."
  • F2 The abstract's "with an estimation precision of approximately 0.01 over a process infidelity range of 0.02 – 0.20" is the calibrated RMSE, defined in the text as the EFS standard deviation divided by the slope and multiplied by the square root of 1 minus r squared, which does not include the fitted intercept of 0.012 ("both with intercept 0.012"). From the fitted lines in Fig. 4 (y=0.94x+0.012 and y=0.93x+0.012, EFS against IRB) the EFS value is about 0.011 above IRB at IRB = 0.02 and within 0.002 of IRB at IRB = 0.20.
  • F3 "confirming the expected null hypothesis that, under diagonal-dominated noise, ε(CCZ)≈ε(I CCZ)": an equivalence read from an agreement with RMSE 0.0159 (1.6 times the Fig 4 figure) and slope 0.92, no width on "≈". And "it follows that the..."
  • F4 The paper prints no run date, job ids, backend calibration records, per-triple EFS or IRB values, IRB fit uncertainties or IRB systematic bound, and has no data or code availability statement. It says only that triples were chosen "excluding qubits and edges flagged as faulty" and that "ibm_kingston yields 204 valid triples", with no count of the flagged items, their source or the date.

  • Read: Full text, version v1, indexed 2026-10-24
  • F1 "the learned channels recover the ground-truth Kraus operators with Choi process fidelity above 0.99": Table I has no null row. The noiseless channel scores F = 0.999 and T = 0.001 on the same truth (our computation from the paper's channel definitions, p = 0.001 in the Table I caption), while the learned channels read T = 0.008822 to 0.02072 at the default bond dimension 8 and up to 0.29 at bond dimension 2, every one above 0.001.
  • F1 "reproduces the device output distribution" / "closely match the experimental data": scored on the training distribution itself (in-sample, 832 parameters, 31 free probabilities). The printed NLL excess of about 0.06 nats (2.87 against the 2.81 bound) is about 63 times the shot-noise floor (our computation) of 31/(2 x 16,384), about 0.00095.
  • F1 Fig 6 baseline: random Kraus noise "of matched magnitude" whose "overall noise magnitude is set by the RMS of the learned parameters" (the authors' own words: "a mild information leakage"). No comparison with a noise model built from IBM's reported ibm_fez figures is shown.
  • F2 "A systematic evaluation across a range of benchmark circuits confirms that this generalization is consistent.": the body says "the majority of points lie above the diagonal" and "The few cases where the random baseline achieves comparable
  • F2 LABS: "This means thatN= 8 is already too difficult given the noise strength." rests on "the learnedCZinfidelity of≈2×10 −2 ... ≈0.98 268 ≈0.5%", a number the paper itself calls an "effective upper bound" and "not ... calibration-grade..."
  • F3 "indicating that the method captures intrinsic device characteristics rather than overfitting to the training circuit" and "confirms": from one training circuit, one named transfer circuit shown as an overlay, and a "majority" claim with no count of the about 40 circuits above the diagonal and no interval on the fidelity differences.
